# aka-claude-tools

> Security defaults for [Claude Code](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code), layered onto an isolated config profile of its own: clean context, locked-down credentials, guarded egress. Nineteen pick-and-choose additions (guard hooks plus a status line and a turn notifier), installed by a shell engine a human runs or a coding agent drives. MIT. Needs `jq` + `bun`.

A coding agent runs shell commands and reaches the network on a developer's behalf. aka-claude-tools adds the guardrails Claude Code doesn't ship with: denying reads of credentials (SSH keys, cloud tokens, `.env`, keychains), blocking `curl … | bash` and edits to shell startup files, matching secret-shaped strings before they leave in a web request, and redacting anything secret-shaped that comes back in a file read, a web fetch, a web search, or an MCP response before the model sees it. Every guard runs **locally**; nothing is uploaded to check it. (Claude Code's own telemetry is left on by default so Remote Control works; the opt-in `telemetry-off` addition disables it.) The guards are defense-in-depth, not a sandbox. A local, redacted audit log records every block/alert/notice (`./install.sh --audit-log`), and an integrity manifest with a `SessionStart` drift check (`./install.sh --audit`) flags a kit file or setting that changed since install.

Two install paths share one source of truth (`config/additions.json`): a human runs `install.sh` interactively, or a coding agent follows `agent-install.md` and drives the same deterministic engine (`./install.sh --apply`, `./install.sh --alias`). A profile is its own `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` launched by a shell alias plus a PATH shim at `<profile>/bin/<name>` (default name `aka-claude`; bare `aka` is reserved for the ai-tc CLI, whose `aka claude` dispatches to the shim), so the kit can be tried in a fresh `~/.claude-aka` without touching the real `~/.claude`.

## For coding agents

- [agent-install.md](https://github.com/akasecurity/claude-tools/blob/main/agent-install.md): The deterministic spec to follow when setting up a profile from inside a user's already-authenticated session. Enumerate existing profiles with `./install.sh --enumerate`, migrate cleanly, then drive `./install.sh --apply` and `./install.sh --alias`. `install.sh` is the sole sanctioned shell-rc writer. Don't improvise. Don't write the rc yourself.
- [agent-uninstall.md](https://github.com/akasecurity/claude-tools/blob/main/agent-uninstall.md): The counterpart spec for cleanly removing a kit-managed profile.
- [config/additions.json](https://github.com/akasecurity/claude-tools/blob/main/config/additions.json): The single source of truth for the addition catalog, defaults, and per-addition build/uninstall logic. Read it; never hardcode an addition into one path only.

## Documentation

- [README.md](https://github.com/akasecurity/claude-tools/blob/main/README.md): What it guards against, quick start, the nineteen additions, the local audit log, the integrity check, profiles, and the threat-model boundaries (what the guards do and don't see).
- [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/akasecurity/claude-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md): Private vulnerability reporting.

## The additions

On by default: `secure-settings` (deny reads of credential paths), `leak-guard` (block secrets in web egress), `command-guard` (block pipe-to-shell, startup-file writes, and secrets in outbound commands; an opt-in `CT_TRUSTED_BOOTSTRAP_URLS` allowlist can exempt specific installer-script URLs from the pipe-to-shell block), `mcp-guard` (MCP server allow/deny policy via `CT_MCP_ALLOW`/`CT_MCP_DENY`, plus a secret scan of MCP tool inputs), `post-guard` (redact secret-shaped values from what a file read, a web fetch, a web search, or an MCP tool call returns, before the model sees it; also warns, never blocks, on prompt-injection phrasing in that returned content), `rtk-safe` (rewrite chatty output to compact summaries; inert until `rtk` is installed), `statusline` (live context-fill and rate-limit gauges), `shell-audit` (on-demand read-only scan of shell startup files), and the nonessential-traffic toggles that don't touch Remote Control: `error-reporting-off` (`DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING`), `feedback-off` (`DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND`), `feedback-survey-off` (`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY`). Opt-in: `sandbox` (enable Claude Code's native OS-level sandbox), `prompt-guard` (warn, never block, on prompt-injection phrasing and other risky content in what the user typed), `wrap-up` (a `/wrap-up` end-of-session handoff that never commits on its own), `secure-deep-research` (privacy-aware web research with per-claim adversarial verification; sensitive topics routed through a self-hosted search instance), `harness-pointer` (a nudge toward the right CLI; ships empty), `notify-osc` (a desktop notification when it's genuinely your turn, quiet while a background task runs; auto-detects the terminal), `telemetry-off` (set `DISABLE_TELEMETRY`; opt-in because it turns off Remote Control), `autoupdater-off` (set `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER`). Each addition stands alone. Take only what you want. Two more pieces run alongside these but aren't in the menu: a local, redacted security-event audit log the guards above write to (`./install.sh --audit-log`), and an internal integrity manifest with a `SessionStart` drift check (`./install.sh --audit`).
